about: E1b (F4, round 2): each test-spec row names on one line the stand-in its oracle rejects, and an assertion that something is absent is paired with an assertion of the exact count or contents, so a version that is right only on the asserted inputs, or drops one rule while keeping totals, fails. Written against 9ed4ec24 (arm T); prompt-only, a row keeps its six keys.

edits.old:
suites says whether the target keeps state); a guard that only checks a file is not RED. "characterisation" if
   it already passes.
edits.new:
suites says whether the target keeps state); a guard that only checks a file is not RED. "characterisation" if
   it already passes. End each row's `red` with one line `Stand-in rejected: <the weaker implementation this
   oracle fails: one rule dropped, right only on these inputs, over the stated budget, or fields valid alone but
   inconsistent together>`; a row no such stand-in fails rejects nothing: strengthen its oracle. Pair every
   assertion that something is absent or rejected with one on the exact count or contents, and check a stated
   budget or limit at its stated value, never at a ceiling the platform enforces first.

edits.old: and one case per documented throw or refusal branch.
edits.new:
and one case per documented throw or refusal branch. In `summary` write `Entry points:` and, per public entry
   point the item adds or changes, the row IDs that call it and the stand-ins they reject.

edits.old: "red": "<how the case fails before the change>"
edits.new: "red": "<how the case fails before the change>; Stand-in rejected: <the simplest wrong implementation this oracle fails>"
